english: For each positive integer $n$, let $S_n=\sin 6^\circ+\sin 12^\circ+\sin 18^\circ+\cdots+\sin\,(6n)^\circ$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{29}\frac{1}{S_n}$ is equal to
hindi: प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना कि $S_n=\sin 6^\circ+\sin 12^\circ+\sin 18^\circ+\cdots+\sin\,(6n)^\circ$ है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{29}\frac{1}{S_n}$ का मान बराबर है
solution: Multiply by $2\sin 3^\circ$ and use product to sum: $2\sin 3^\circ\sin(6k)^\circ=\cos(6k-3)^\circ-\cos(6k+3)^\circ$, which telescopes
solution_full: Closed form of $S_n$ (angles in AP, common difference $6^\circ$). By the product-to-sum formula $2\sin A\sin B=\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)$:
Adding for $k=1$ to $n$, consecutive terms cancel: $2\sin 3^\circ\,S_n=\cos 3^\circ-\cos(6n+3)^\circ$.
Sum to product on the right: $\cos 3^\circ-\cos(6n+3)^\circ=2\sin(3n+3)^\circ\sin(3n)^\circ$. Hence $S_n=\dfrac{\sin(3n)^\circ\sin(3n+3)^\circ}{\sin 3^\circ}$.
For $1\le n\le 29$ the angles $3n^\circ$ and $(3n+3)^\circ$ lie in $(0^\circ,90^\circ]$, so $S_n>0$ and every term $\dfrac{1}{S_n}$ is defined.
Now $\cot x-\cot y=\dfrac{\sin(y-x)}{\sin x\sin y}$. With $x=(3n)^\circ$, $y=(3n+3)^\circ$: $\cot(3n)^\circ-\cot(3n+3)^\circ=\dfrac{\sin 3^\circ}{\sin(3n)^\circ\sin(3n+3)^\circ}=\dfrac{1}{S_n}$.
Keeping an extra factor $\dfrac{1}{\sin 3^\circ}$ by mistake gives (B); (C) and (D) are close numbers but wrong.
originality_note: New: the reciprocals of the PARTIAL SUMS of an AP sine series telescope, because S_n = sin(3n) sin(3n+3)/sin 3 is exactly the denominator of a cot difference (way 5). Closest known: sum of 1/(sin k sin(k+1)) (2025-P2-Q15, AIME 2000 II-15). Different because: the product is not given; it appears only after summing the AP series, and the series itself is summed by product-to-sum.
blueprint_concepts: Summation of trigonometric series with angles in AP
Telescoping trigonometric series using tan/cot identities

concept_use.Sum-to-product and product-to-sum transf: 2 sin 3 sin 6k = cos(6k-3) - cos(6k+3), and cos 3 - cos(6n+3) = 2 sin 3n sin(3n+3), give the closed form of S_n.
concept_use.Summation of trigonometric series with a: S_n is the sum of sines with angles 6, 12, ..., 6n in AP; its closed form sin(3n) sin(3n+3)/sin 3 is the heart of the question.
concept_use.Telescoping trigonometric series using t: 1/S_n = cot 3n - cot(3n+3), so the 29 terms collapse to cot 3 - cot 90.
